deferred_source_units.reason: The heading concerning the eighth and the David attribution are preserved; a repeated generic title alone does not receive a separate substantive connection.
The assurance that the Lord will keep and preserve us from this generation and for ever is preserved; no more particular additional counterpart is retained beyond that common assurance of protection.
The ungodly walking around and the Lord holding humanity in high regard according to His height are preserved without replacing the second clause with a familiar exaltation-of-vileness reading.
The generic liturgical heading is preserved without separate connection credit.
The repeated questions about inner counsel, daily heart-pain and the enemy being raised remain distinct; no particular episode or additional counterpart is established.
The poor man’s shamed counsel and hope in the Lord are preserved; no specific counsel or historical poor person is identified by a generic poverty-and-hope comparison.
The inscription and plea for guarding because of hope in the Lord are preserved; no additional specific connection is retained from the general protection formula.
The holy ones in His land and His wonderful purposes among them are not assigned a particular named group or event by analogy.

The gatherings of bloodshed and refusal to remember names remain as supplied. They are not rewritten as blood drink-offerings or assigned the identity of other gods; the naming comparison remains a separate zero-credit candidate.
The understanding given by the Lord and the kidneys’ discipline until night remain exact; no definite prophetic revelation or outside identity for that inward discipline is supplied.
Human deeds, words of God’s lips and hard paths are preserved without changing the hard paths into a familiar reference to paths of violent people.
Calling, being heard and asking for an inclined ear are preserved; the general prayer-attention formula alone receives no additional connection credit.
The enemies surrounding the speaker’s soul remain unnamed; a generic encirclement image does not identify a particular siege or hostile assembly.
The statement that they shut up their fat is not silently converted into a description of unfeeling hearts; no particular counterpart to the complete wording is retained.
The eyes set to turn aside toward the earth are not rewritten into an explicit plan to throw the speaker to the ground; the exact relationship of the clauses remains unresolved.
The command to intercept and trip the enemies and the request concerning God’s sword are preserved. The ungodly man is not identified as God’s sword from a different familiar wording.

The few, earthly life, hidden things, filled belly, sons and remains for infants remain exact; they are not harmonized into a familiar statement that worldly people have their portion only in this life.
Appearance before God in righteousness and satisfaction when His glory appears are preserved without adding awakening from death or identifying a particular resurrection event.
The generic heading supplies no separate substantive counterpart.
Day’s utterance to day and night’s announcement to night remain the particular poetic sequence; a general creation-teaches motif does not establish an additional close counterpart in this pass.

The actual statement that there are no utterances or words whose voices are not heard is preserved. It is not changed into wordless or inaudible speech; the direct Romans quotation is retained for the following source unit.
The servant’s keeping and great recompense are preserved; no particular reward is identified from a generic obedience-and-blessing passage.

The source asks to be spared from others and their rule. Others is not silently replaced by presumptuous sins; the proposed comparison with Romans’ explicit rule of sin remains unresolved and earns zero credit.
The generic heading is preserved without a separate supported connection.
Their being fettered and falling, contrasted with our rising and being set upright, is preserved without identifying a particular battle or importing another passage’s named parties.
The generic heading is preserved without separate substantive connection credit.
The king’s glory, salvation and promised magnificence are preserved; a general statement that God grants honor does not furnish a particular additional match here.

The first clause asks that the addressed person’s hand be found by enemies; the second asks that the right hand find all who hate the addressee. Neither the direction of the first action nor the unspecified addressee is replaced by familiar wording.
The closing exaltation and promise of song for God’s mighty acts are preserved; generic praise of divine power alone is not counted as another particular connection.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Both texts concern names not being recalled or heard from the mouth, but Exodus explicitly names other gods while the psalm does not resolve the identity of its names. Its gatherings of bloodshed are not converted into drink-offerings to supply that identity.

The source speaks of others not ruling over the speaker, while Romans explicitly names sin as the would-be ruler. The shared rule-over language does not establish that the psalm’s others means presumptuous sins or sin itself.
